courthouses.name: Trinity County Superior Court — Main Courthouse
courthouses.hours: All divisions and Collections: Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. (Jury Services closed 12–1)
courthouses.note: The only courthouse the court lists. Criminal, traffic, juvenile, civil, family and probate are all handled here. Clerk email courtclerks@trinitycounty.org. Mailing: PO Box 1258, Weaverville, CA 96093. Fines can also be paid at Trinity County Probation/Collections, 333 Tom Bell Road.

public_defenders.name: Trinity County Public Defender (contract counsel)
public_defenders.note: Trinity County has no county Public Defender department in its official directory. It contracts indigent defense: the county's 2024 RFP sought a firm/consortium to provide primary public defense plus at least two levels of conflict counsel in felony, misdemeanor and juvenile cases. The court's Criminal page: ask the judge at arraignment to appoint the Public Defender; the judge decides how much (if any) of the fee you must repay.

legal_aid.name: Legal Services of Northern California — Eureka Office
legal_aid.serves: Low-income residents of Del Norte, Humboldt and Trinity counties
legal_aid.what: Civil legal aid including criminal record remedies (record clearing), citation defense for people experiencing homelessness, housing, public benefits, health, education. Not criminal defense on open cases.
legal_aid.note: 123 Third Street, Eureka, CA 95501. Evening intake message line (866) 815-5990.

probation.name: Trinity County Probation — Weaverville
probation.note: Fax (530) 623-1237. Also houses the Collections Department (court fines).

jails.name: Trinity County Correctional Facility (Detention Facility)
jails.phone_note: Fax (530) 623-3926. Mail for people inside: PO Box 1119, Weaverville, CA 96093. Sheriff Records Lobby (101 Memorial Dr.): (530) 623-2611.
jails.note: County's only adult jail. 'both' is based on the Sheriff's handbook classification plan, which assigns housing by sex (among other factors). Visits are non-contact, twice weekly per unit (A: Wed 2:30–4:30 & Sat 7–9 p.m.; B: Mon 2:30–4:30 & Thu 7–9; C: Thu 2:30–4:30 & Sun 7–9; D: Tue 2:30–4:30 & Fri 7–9; Holding: Wed 7–9 & Sun 2:30–4:30) per handbook revised May 2023; max 2 visitors, photo ID. Video visits are free from the jail lobby. Handbook says new arrests usually go to court within two court days, typically in the afternoon. Weaverville is the county's only courthouse (nearest, not confirmed as the transport destination by the Sheriff).
